findings.action: Label in ranked order. Do not quote review counts as detections.
findings.evidence: Fusion marks 4 of 15 evidence-covered 2026 recordings and 3 of 10 evidence-covered 2023 recordings for review. Marks come from within-cohort percentile ranks cut at fused support >= 2/3, so roughly the top third is selected whatever the absolute evidence.
findings.interpretation: Signal and correlation run the same autocorrelation on the same channels, and DTW borrows the signal period. Fusion is effectively one evidence source and a priority ranking, not a count of recordings with recurrence.
findings.title: Fusion ranks recordings for review; it does not detect recurrence

findings.action: Calibrate recurrence scores against a surrogate null and report per-recording p-values before using the flag.
findings.evidence: Review flag fires on 25.0% of 4 control recordings versus 44.4% of 9 non-control recordings in 2026, and on 50.0% of 2 control recordings versus 12.5% of 8 non-control recordings in 2023. Minimum rank-1 cycle count is 2.02 and 2.23: lag is capped at half the duration, so the `cycle_count >= 2` gate never rejects and the flag is correlation >= 0.25 alone.
findings.interpretation: Stationary or low-dynamics recordings pass about as often as driving at these sample sizes. The threshold has no demonstrated discriminative power.
findings.title: Signal flag does not separate controls from driving

findings.action: Require peaks well inside the search range, or record sessions spanning several expected laps.
findings.evidence: Rank-1 signal lags at or above 80% of the search ceiling (half the duration, capped at 120 s): 9 of 13 (69%) in 2026 and 3 of 10 (30%) in 2023.
findings.interpretation: A peak at the ceiling compares roughly two halves of one recording and is edge-prone. It should not be read as a lap period.
findings.title: Many candidate periods sit at the search ceiling

findings.action: Do not quote the shared 2023 period as a lap time. Treat half-period values as harmonics.
findings.evidence: 2023: 5 of 8 non-control recordings carry a signal or correlation period within 10% of 45.3 s; 2 more sit near half that period, a likely harmonic. 2026: 5 of 11 non-control recordings carry a signal or correlation period within 10% of 16.0 s; that period sits at the 15 s search floor, so it is a likely artifact.
findings.interpretation: Separate recordings agreeing on one period would be stronger evidence than any per-recording score, but these periods carry no null calibration and locate no boundary. The calibrated physics test does not confirm them.
findings.title: 2023 recordings converge near 45 s; 2026 recordings do not converge on a usable period

findings.action: Read these p-values as upper bounds on evidence. Tighten the null until benchmark false positives match nominal before trusting any single detection.
findings.evidence: Block-shuffle null, 199 surrogates per recording. 2026 (motor speed): Distance domain: 1 of 8 driving recordings reach p < 0.05 (1 after false-discovery control, 3 at the search ceiling); benchmark recovers 98% of tiled laps and flags 25% of unrelated segments over 40 trials. Time domain: 3 of 9 driving recordings reach p < 0.05 (3 after false-discovery control, 3 at the search ceiling); benchmark recovers 98% of tiled laps and flags 20% of unrelated segments over 40 trials. 2023 (yaw rate): Time domain: 0 of 8 driving recordings reach p < 0.05 (0 after false-discovery control, 0 at the search ceiling); benchmark recovers 95% of tiled laps and flags 32% of unrelated segments over 40 trials.
findings.interpretation: The detector recovers planted laps, but its null is optimistic: unrelated real segments pass well above the nominal rate. No significant share in real recordings is distinguishable from that benchmark false-positive rate (smallest one-sided binomial p = 0.26), so neither cohort shows lap recurrence inside a recording. Resampling 2026 motor speed onto distance did not expose laps that time-domain analysis missed.
findings.title: Calibrated physics detector finds no recurrence beyond its false-positive rate

findings.action: Use aligned runs as provisional lap labels. Replace the global pace factor with time-warped alignment for sector times, and log wheel speed or GPS to fix start and finish.
findings.evidence: 8 driving runs segmented from 7 recordings trace one course: pairwise yaw-rate correlation after pace and offset alignment has median 0.83 and minimum 0.73, against a shuffled-run null with 95th percentile 0.42 and maximum 0.47 over 140 draws; 100% of 28 pairs beat the null. Aligned lap times span 80.1-108.5 s, median 86.6 s.
findings.interpretation: Each long 2023 recording holds one run of the same course, two in the longest, so the lap unit is the run. That is why no method found recurrence inside a recording. Lap times are relative to the reference run's span under one global pace factor; start and finish lines are not observed, and the null shares the optimism measured for the recurrence detector, though the margin here is wide.
findings.title: 2023 runs repeat one course: laps recur across recordings, not inside them

findings.action: Retest DTW against manually labeled lap pairs and unrelated hard negatives with leave-one-recording-out evaluation.
findings.evidence: Held-out match rates are 50.0% (95% recording-level bootstrap 0%–100%; 16 pairs from 3 recordings; includes 50% chance) for 2026 and 70.0% (95% recording-level bootstrap 50%–90%; 20 pairs from 2 recordings; includes 50% chance) for 2023.
findings.interpretation: Held-out intervals include chance for: 2026 EV drive day, 2023 AiM event. Pairs are overlapping windows inside few recordings, and DTW uses signal-derived periods, so agreement cannot count as independent confirmation.
findings.title: DTW held-out support is not distinguishable from chance

findings.action: Use interpolation only below a validated gap limit and retain an imputation mask.
findings.evidence: Best short-gap median normalized RMSE is 0.20 for 2026 and 0.54 for 2023; 0.5 s gaps rise to 0.30 and 2.45.
findings.interpretation: Interior interpolation can repair isolated samples but cannot create missing dynamics or timing truth.
findings.title: Interpolation repairs short gaps only

findings.action: Do not use these embeddings as pseudo-labels. Keep temporal resolution in the encoder and add hard negatives before retesting.
findings.evidence: Effective rank: masked 1.03, contrastive 3.31, autoencoder 4.01 of 8 for 2026; masked 1.03, contrastive 4.34, autoencoder 6.28 of 8 for 2023.
findings.interpretation: The masked encoder ends in global average pooling and decodes through one linear layer, so a 10 s window cannot be rebuilt from the pooled code. Collapse is architectural, from one untuned configuration, and says nothing about the data. Contrastive and autoencoder codes do not collapse.
findings.title: Masked-reconstruction encoder collapses by design

findings.action: Keep PCA as baseline; revisit autoencoders only with a task-linked validation target.
findings.evidence: Test MSE ratios versus PCA are 1.28 for 2026 and 1.03 for 2023; values above 1 are worse.
findings.interpretation: One configuration (8 latent dimensions, 25 epochs, no tuning). Ratios carry no interval, so values near 1 are not distinguishable from PCA.
findings.title: Untuned autoencoder does not beat PCA

findings.action: Do not promote GRU residuals to labels. Predict deltas, evaluate multi-second horizons, and tune on the validation split before concluding.
findings.evidence: Test MSE ratios versus persistence are 1.91 for 2026 and 7.81 for 2023.
findings.interpretation: One configuration: 16 hidden units, 20 epochs, no tuning or early stopping. A model that loses to copying the last sample is undertrained; this is not evidence that sequence models fail on this data.
findings.title: Untuned GRU does not beat persistence

findings.action: Check stability with a recording-level bootstrap and drop redundant channels before using clusters as strata.
findings.evidence: Training selects k=3 with silhouette 0.862 for 2026 and 0.667 for 2023; seed ARI is 1.000 and 1.000. 2026: largest cluster holds 94.6% of 500 windows, minority clusters draw on 3 of 21 recordings, and the largest cluster mixes 105 control windows with 368 non-control windows. 2023: largest cluster holds 66.9% of 936 windows, minority clusters draw on 7 of 18 recordings, and the largest cluster mixes 115 control windows with 511 non-control windows.
findings.interpretation: A dominant cluster that mixes controls with driving is not an operating regime, and high silhouette can come from a few outlying windows. Seed ARI tests initialization only, not resampling stability.
findings.title: Cluster structure is dominated by one regime

findings.action: Fuse evidence by method family and preserve disagreement instead of averaging all scores.
findings.evidence: Strongest recording correlations are Autoencoder–Sequence at rho=0.97 for 2026 and Autoencoder–Sequence at rho=0.95 for 2023.
findings.interpretation: Correlated reconstruction and sequence errors reflect shared signal difficulty, not independent lap agreement.
findings.title: Strong method correlations mostly expose shared behavior

limitations: No independent lap boundaries, start-line beacon, GPS position, or official timing truth are present.
2023 elapsed time is inferred from validated 20 Hz sampling because source time cells are blank.
2026 timestamps are regular at 10 Hz; interpolation adds no higher-frequency information.
DTW depends on signal-derived candidate periods, and learned-method windows overlap.
Methods 1-8 have no null calibration: scores are compared with fixed thresholds or within-cohort ranks, never with a surrogate distribution.
The validation split is never used for model or threshold selection.
Evaluation uses one fixed recording split; held-out sets hold two to five recordings per cohort.
Clusters are not validated as regimes, lap phases, or track sectors.
next_actions: Label boundaries in fusion-ranked order, starting with the 7 top-ranked recordings.
Record lap beacon or GPS truth during the next event.
Replace the global pace factor with time-warped alignment and derive sector times from aligned 2023 runs.
Tighten the physics null until benchmark false positives match nominal alpha.
Evaluate boundary error, lap-count error, precision, and recall with leave-one-recording-out splits and recording-level intervals.
Keep PCA and persistence as mandatory baselines.
Retain interpolation masks and reject gaps beyond validated limits.
